To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Penrose’s theory was not intended as a source of strategic prescriptions for how to create rents and that, although she did not explicitly state that firms should be concerned about the sustainability of rents, the implications for the resource-based view of the firm are clear: the theory of the growth of the firm is a theory of how firms grow, not a theory of how to create rents.
Edith Penrose did not intend her work to provide a basis for the resource-based theory of competitive advantage.
Penrose’s work was not intended to be a theory of the firm, nor a theory of the growth of the firm, but rather a description of the growth process.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: what are the factors that affect the rate at which a firm grows?
the development of a theory of the growth of the firm, a theory which is based on the analysis of the processes of growth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Penrose’s work has not provided a theory of the firm, nor has it provided a theory of strategy, and it has certainly not provided a theory about how to create rents.
Edith Penrose has not contributed directly to the resourcebased view of the firm.
the RBV is not a theory, but a research agenda.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it was a great pleasure for us to have been able to work with Edith Penrose and to have been able, in some small way, to repay the debt that all of us owe her.
we are not interested in how to make a firm grow, but in how a firm that is growing makes its growth possible.
we are trying to understand the nature of the firm, and the process by which it grows.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strategy field should be careful not to over-interpret the work of Edith Penrose and other scholars in the strategy domain.
Edith Penrose did not aim to provide useful strategy advice.
the resource-based view is an intellectual construction built upon the foundations laid by Edith Penroses’ work.
